tools.name: create_bill
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to create and share an itemized bill for a restaurant meal or shared purchase, with a link where participants select their own items and calculate their shares. Accept items from a receipt photo, typed list or plain-language description; no receipt or separately supplied

tools.name: get_current_user_profile
tools.description: Returns the authenticated user's id, full_name, email and created_at for the bill UI to identify their own item selections. Requires OAuth and uses the user identity from the bearer token. This read-only helper is intended for calls from the app UI.

tools.name: set_bill_selections_batch
tools.description: Use this when the connected user asks to select, change or clear their own items on an existing shared bill, such as one pizza portion and one tip share, for calculating their personal share. Saves absolute item selection quantities for that user; it does not change bill items, prices or the total.

tools.name: update_bill
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to edit an existing shared bill: correct an item, rename it, add or remove purchases, add tips by participant count, or divide a shared dish into selectable portions. Replaces the complete content of a public bill owned by the connected user, whether created from a receip

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_bill" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when the user wants to create and share an itemized bill for a restaurant meal or shared purchase, with a link where participants select their own item…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_current_user_profile" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_current_user_profile, update_bill · Private data: create_bill, get_current_user_profile · Public sink: create_bill, get_current_user_profile, set_bill_selections_batch, update_bill · Destructive: update_bill.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_current_user_profile, update_bill · Private data: create_bill, get_current_user_profile · Public sink: create_bill, get_current_user_profile, set_bill_selections_batch, update_bill · Destructive: update_bill

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
